latest_action.text: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 694.

c.summary: H.R. 9329, titled the 'SEC Reform and Restructuring Act', makes several organizational, procedural, and regulatory changes to the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and related bodies. Key areas include enhanced cost-benefit analysis requirements for SEC regulations, increased congressional oversight and testimony, a Government Accountability Office (GAO) audit of SEC cybersecurity and IT, the transfer of the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board into an office within the SEC, recurring GAO studies on major rules, minimum public comment periods, clarity on counting multiple violations for enforcement penalties, and internal SEC organizational restructuring.

c.summary: H.R. 9203, the Student Protection and University Accountability Act, requires colleges and universities that participate in federal student aid programs to establish specific processes for investigating complaints related to Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964. It sets deadlines for schools to respond to complaints, requires them to keep records, mandates public posting of federal civil rights awareness materials, and penalizes schools that fail to comply for two consecutive years by making them ineligible for federal student aid. Additionally, the bill requires the Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights to give bimonthly briefings and reports to Congress and restricts how it dismisses or delays certain complaints.

c.label: H.R. 6422
c.title: American Water Stewardship Act

latest_action.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.

c.summary: H.R. 6422, the American Water Stewardship Act, reauthorizes and updates several Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) water quality protection and restoration programs through fiscal year 2031. It extends funding authorization for programs covering the Great Lakes, Long Island Sound, the Columbia River Basin, the National Estuary Program, and coastal water monitoring. It also adds the Mississippi Sound to the National Estuary Program, modifies eligibility and cost-sharing rules for the San Francisco Bay program, allows beach water grants to be used to identify specific contamination sources, restricts funding to certain foreign entities of concern, and requires a government accountability report on EPA geographic programs.

c.label: S. 1498
c.title: Halting Ownership and Non-Ethical Stock Transactions (HONEST) Act

latest_action.text: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 294.

c.summary: The S. 1498 bill, titled the Halting Ownership and Non-Ethical Stock Transactions (HONEST) Act, prohibits the President, Vice President, Members of Congress, and their spouses and dependent children from owning, purchasing, or selling certain investments, such as individual stocks, commodities, futures, and digital assets. Covered individuals must divest from these restricted investments upon starting a new term or within specified timelines, and they are prohibited from maintaining qualified blind trusts. The bill establishes civil penalties for noncompliance, requires financial disclosures and compliance notices to be published online in searchable databases, and sets new reporting and penalty rules related to federal financial benefits and existing disclosure requirements.

c.summary: H.R. 10076, the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, imposes extensive economic and financial sanctions, trade restrictions, and duty increases related to the Russian Federation and extends the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996. The bill targets Russian government officials, specific financial institutions and energy projects, defense industrial base suppliers, and vessels circumventing existing sanctions. It also prohibits certain investments, securities listings, sovereign debt purchases, fund transfers, and energy and uranium imports involving Russia. Additionally, the legislation places duties on imports from foreign countries that purchase Russian crude oil or natural gas or help evade sanctions. It includes specific exceptions for humanitarian assistance, intelligence activities, and NASA operations, and extends the expiration date of the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 through 2031.

c.summary: The SAFE Banking Act of 2026 creates legal protections for banks, credit unions, and insurance companies that provide financial services to state-sanctioned marijuana businesses and legitimate hemp businesses. c.summary: H.R. 9773, titled the 'Permanent Trump Secure Border Act,' proposes comprehensive changes to U.S. immigration, asylum, border inspection, and parole laws. c.title: Lower Costs, More Transparency Act of 2026

latest_action.text: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 45 - 0.

c.summary: H.R. 9393, the "Lower Costs, More Transparency Act of 2026," promotes price transparency across the U.S. health care sector. Beginning January 1, 2028, hospitals, clinical diagnostic laboratories, imaging providers and suppliers, ambulatory surgical centers, and group health plans (as well as health insurance issuers) must publicly disclose standard charges, prices, and rates in consumer-friendly and machine-readable formats. The legislation establishes compliance monitoring, enforcement procedures, civil monetary penalties for noncompliance, and specific reporting requirements for federal agencies.

c.summary: The Don't Sell Kids' Data Act of 2025 prohibits data brokers from collecting, using, maintaining, selling, or transferring the personal data of children (under 13) and teens (ages 13 to 17) when they know the individual is a minor. c.title: Main Street Depositor Protection Act

latest_action.text: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

c.summary: The Main Street Depositor Protection Act amends the Federal Deposit Insurance Act and the Federal Credit Union Act to provide federal deposit insurance for certain noninterest-bearing transaction accounts. It directs the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) to issue a rule establishing a maximum insurance amount between the standard maximum and $5,000,000 for these accounts, with certain exclusions for global systemically important bank holding companies and foreign bank branches. Credit unions are also included under parallel rules. Furthermore, the bill outlines a 10-year transition period for phasing in the calculation of these insured deposits and exempts certain smaller depository institutions from specific special assessments during this transition.

latest_action.text: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 241.

c.summary: The STOP China and Russia Act of 2025 directs the U.S. President to impose economic and travel sanctions on foreign persons—specifically individuals or entities from China or Russia—who knowingly facilitate military or defense-industrial cooperation between the two nations. This includes Chinese support for Russia's defense base and war in Ukraine, as well as Russian support that enhances China's military capabilities for operations in the Taiwan Strait. The bill also requires the executive branch to develop a coordinated international strategy with allies and submit regular reports to Congress.

c.title: NDO Fairness Act of 2025

latest_action.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

c.summary: The NDO Fairness Act of 2025 modifies the requirements and procedures for the government to obtain nondisclosure orders (NDOs) under the Stored Communications Act. These orders temporarily stop communication and remote computing service providers from telling customers or subscribers that the government has sought their records or electronic communications. The bill raises the legal standards required to get an NDO, limits the duration of NDOs, introduces mandatory court reviews, requires notice to targets when NDOs expire, and mandates annual reporting by the Department of Justice.

c.title: Power Plant Reliability Act of 2025

latest_action.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.

c.summary: The Power Plant Reliability Act of 2025 modifies how the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) handles power plant retirements and grid reliability. It allows transmission organizations and state commissions to ask FERC to keep power plants open if closing them would harm the reliability of the bulk power system. The bill requires power plant owners to give five years of advance notice before retiring a generating unit and exempts actions taken to comply with FERC reliability orders from environmental laws.

c.title: Unlocking our Domestic LNG Potential Act of 2025

latest_action.text: Read the second time. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 286.

c.summary: The Unlocking our Domestic LNG Potential Act of 2025 removes certain Department of Energy approval requirements and restrictions on importing and exporting natural gas. It gives the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission exclusive authority to approve or deny applications for natural gas import and export facilities, such as liquefied natural gas terminals, and requires the Commission to deem such imports and exports consistent with the public interest. The bill does not limit presidential authority under existing laws and emergencies to prohibit imports or exports involving sanctioned persons or state sponsors of terrorism.

latest_action.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

c.summary: The PILLAR Act extends and updates the State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program through fiscal year 2035. The bill broadens what the grant money can protect by including operational technology and artificial intelligence systems owned, maintained, or operated by state, local, and tribal governments. It places restrictions on purchasing software or hardware from foreign entities of concern or products that do not align with Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency guidance. Additionally, the legislation increases federal cost-share percentages for entities that implement multi-factor authentication tools by a specific date, mandates annual reporting on sustaining programs after grants expire, and requires outreach to rural and small-population local governments regarding no-cost cybersecurity offerings.

c.label: H.R. 1486
c.title: Economic Espionage Prevention Act

latest_action.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.

c.summary: The Economic Espionage Prevention Act authorizes the President to impose visa bans and property-blocking sanctions on foreign adversary entities that engage in economic or industrial espionage regarding U.S. trade secrets, provide material support to foreign military or intelligence entities, or violate U.S. export control laws. It defines foreign adversaries using existing federal regulations (naming China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, Cuba, and the Maduro regime of Venezuela). Additionally, the bill limits certain standard exemptions under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act regarding information imports/exports, international travel, and personal communications when dealing with a declared national emergency or involving bulk sensitive personal data and connected software application source code. The bill also requires a report from the Secretary of State detailing Chinese component supplies to Russia's defense industrial base.

c.summary: The Expanding Whistleblower Protections for Contractors Act of 2026 amends current laws concerning federal, defense, and NASA contractors, subcontractors, grantees, and personal service workers. It expands protections against retaliation for refusing to obey unlawful orders or for disclosing information regarding gross mismanagement, gross waste of funds, abuse of authority, or dangers to public health and safety. It also clarifies that executive branch officials do not have the authority to request a reprisal against protected individuals, allows for proposed disciplinary actions against officials who make such requests, and prohibits the waiver of these rights under any public or private agreement, including pre-dispute arbitration agreements.

latest_action.text: Received in the Senate. Read twice. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 465.

c.summary: H.R. 5578 expands whistleblower protections for federal contractors, subcontractors, grant recipients, and personal service workers—including state, local, and tribal government entities and their employees—under both Department of Defense and civilian federal contracts. c.label: H.R. 4626
c.title: Home Appliance Protection and Affordability Act

latest_action.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.

c.summary: The Home Appliance Protection and Affordability Act changes how the Department of Energy (DOE) creates and updates energy and water efficiency standards for household appliances and other consumer products. The bill adds strict new requirements the DOE must follow before issuing rules, such as proving that a standard will not increase net costs for consumers, will pay for itself within three years through utility savings, and will not reduce product performance or eliminate certain fuel-type products from the market. It also sets rules for revoking standards through a petition process, prohibits new standards for distribution transformers, requires public disclosure of certain DOE meetings, and allows specific new standards for clothes washers and dishwashers.
